entry_state: Information is valuable through timely decisions, and ambiguous histories require explicit objectives and terminal rules. Economic numerical methods must solve the stated timing and policy-consistent equations. Squared single-draw residuals add a variance penalty; constraints, total derivatives, units and the sampled state domain each change what a solver computes.
exit_state: Policy transfer needs feasible actions and information, not just an adapted learned process. Off-policy states and multiple equilibria limit conclusions from residuals. Validation therefore separates implementation, model coherence and empirical adequacy, then challenges evidence admission, hidden history, state memory, information timing, scenario meaning and financing cash conventions.

observations.finding: The singleton-policy example h(x)=clip(x,0,1), Q(x,a)=a and point masses at 1 and 0 has value difference 1 although state-Lipschitz constant zero would predict zero without feasibility of the transferred policy. The paper edition and code support boundary is explicit. Off-policy loss pair (1,100) versus (1,0) yields regret 99 under the approximation-selected action.
observations.disposition: retain local counterexamples; source theorem rejection remains restricted to the stated retained edition and premises
